title: Rigidity of derived tensor models on cochain representatives
statement:
Let $(\mathcal S,J)$ be a site small relative to a coefficient universe $w$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings in that universe. Use the abelian category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its category $\operatorname{Ch}(R)$ of unbounded cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and its unbounded derived category $D(R)$ with cochain localization $Q:\operatorname{Ch}(R)\to D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal P$ be the full subcategory of cochain complexes that are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and whose terms are flat module sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]; flatness here means exactness of tensoring with the sheafified sectionwise tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $\iota:\mathcal P\to\operatorname{Ch}(R)$ and $q=Q\iota$. Let $t$ denote signed direct-sum total tensor of complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and let $T:D(R)\times D(R)\to D(R)$ be the tensor model obtained by localization on flat-term K-flat homotopy representatives [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], with its given natural representative comparison there.

There is a natural isomorphism $r:Q\,t(\iota\times\iota)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(q\times q)$ obtained from that homotopy representative comparison using the canonical factorization $Q\cong Q_h\circ\pi$, where $\pi$ is the homotopy quotient and $Q_h$ its derived localization. It uses the same sheaf tensor and the same flatness predicate on cochain representatives. For every bifunctor $T':D(R)\times D(R)\to D(R)$ equipped with a natural isomorphism $r':Q\,t(\iota\times\iota)\xrightarrow{\sim}T'(q\times q)$, there is a unique natural isomorphism $e:T\xrightarrow{\sim}T'$ satisfying $r;e(q\times q)=r'$. Moreover, for every category $\mathcal E$, precomposition with $q\times q$ is fully faithful on functors $D(R)\times D(R)\to\mathcal E$. No functorial choice of K-flat resolutions is required.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal H$ be the full subcategory of $K(R)$ used in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Its objects are precisely the same complexes as those of $\mathcal P$: K-flatness and flatness of terms have literally the predicates of [def-pc-kflat-complex] and [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Use the presentation of the homotopy category with complexes as objects and homotopy classes of chain maps as morphisms. The restricted quotient $p:\mathcal P\to\mathcal H$ is identity on these objects and surjective on every morphism set. For functors $A,B:\mathcal H\times\mathcal H\to\mathcal E$, a transformation between their restrictions along $p\times p$ defines its component at $(P_1,P_2)$ by that same component. Its naturality for a pair of homotopy classes follows by representing each class by a chain map and applying the given naturality square; the images under $A$ and $B$ depend only on the classes. Conversely restriction keeps every component. Thus precomposition with $p\times p$ is fully faithful, for arbitrary $\mathcal E$. This is the direct quotient-definition argument, not an assertion that $p$ is faithful.

source.place: Tag 013H (definition-complexes-notation, clause (5)): homotopy classes of maps; restriction to the same objects

proof.text: Write $\kappa:\mathcal H\to K(R)$ and $\ell=Q_h\kappa$. The last clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] states that, for every $\mathcal E$, restriction along $\ell\times\ell$ gives a bijection on natural transformations between any two functors $D(R)\times D(R)\to\mathcal E$. Compose this bijection with the bijection in Step 1. The result is full faithfulness of restriction along $(\ell p)\times(\ell p)$. The cochain/homotopy factorization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $\alpha:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_h\pi$, hence $\alpha\iota:q\xrightarrow{\sim}\ell p$. Conjugation by the images of $(\alpha\iota)\times(\alpha\iota)$ under the two target functors is a bijection between the corresponding sets of transformations. This proves the claimed full faithfulness for $q\times q$, including arbitrary transformations and arbitrary target categories.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding construction); homotopy representative transformation descent in lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent

proof.text: Let $t_h:K(R)\times K(R)\to K(R)$ be the homotopy total tensor and let $\rho:Q_h t_h(\kappa\times\kappa)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(\ell\times\ell)$ be the given natural representative comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. That node uses the signed direct-sum tensor of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]; therefore $\pi t\cong t_h(\pi\times\pi)$ is its cochain-to-homotopy tensor comparison. Define the component $r_{P_1,P_2}$ as the composite $$Q t(P_1,P_2)\xrightarrow{\alpha_{t(P_1,P_2)}}Q_h\pi t(P_1,P_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_h t_h(pP_1,pP_2)\xrightarrow{\rho_{pP_1,pP_2}}T(\ell pP_1,\ell pP_2)\xrightarrow{T(\alpha_{P_1}^{-1},\alpha_{P_2}^{-1})}T(qP_1,qP_2).$$ Every arrow is a component of a natural isomorphism, so their composite is a natural isomorphism with the required source and target. Both tensor constructions use the sheafification of sectionwise tensor in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and differential $d_1\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d_2$; the representative categories in Step 1 use the same flatness predicate. Thus the construction changes neither tensor nor representative conditions.

proof.text: Fix $(T\prime,r\prime)$ as in the statement, and put $F=q\times q$. In usual composition notation let $a=r\prime\circ r^{-1}:T\circ F\xrightarrow{\sim}T\prime\circ F$. By the fullness proved in Step 2 there are natural transformations $e:T\to T\prime$ and $d:T\prime\to T$ restricting respectively to $a$ and $a^{-1}$. Restriction takes their composites to $a^{-1}\circ a$ and $a\circ a^{-1}$, which are identities. Faithfulness from Step 2 therefore gives $d\circ e=1_T$ and $e\circ d=1_{T\prime}$. Hence $e$ is a natural isomorphism. Its restriction is $r\prime\circ r^{-1}$, so $r;eF=r\prime$. Any other compatible natural isomorphism has that same restriction by cancellation of $r$ and equals $e$ by faithfulness; equality of the forward transformations determines equality of the isomorphisms. The argument uses the already given homotopy tensor model and natural comparison, quotient classes, and bijections on transformation sets. At no stage does it choose K-flat resolutions functorially.
